text:
The Rangers come to Toronto on two days' rest after a 5-2 win over Anaheim, their third win in their last five (3-1-1). The Maple Leafs played one night earlier, a 6-2 win at Columbus in which Marshall Rifai scored his first NHL goal, and they are still without John Tavares and Chris Tanev. With Tavares out, Colton Sissons has moved in beside William Nylander and Gavin McKenna, and McKenna has taken a spot on the first power-play unit. Auston Matthews is two points from 800 for his career, though that milestone is not in our numbers.

The matchup in chance creation tilts New York's way. At five on five, the Rangers have taken 52% of the expected goals (a measure of shot quality) in their games, and Toronto 43%. The Leafs also take about 4.4 penalties a game, which keeps handing out power plays. In net, Dylan Garand (projected) has saved 4.2 goals above expected this season, with a .929 save percentage. Sergei Bobrovsky (projected) is at +5.3 despite a .901 mark, though he was 13.5 goals below expected last season.

Matthews has a 37% chance to score by our numbers, and Nylander 36%. For the Rangers, Pavel Dorofeyev is at 36% and Mika Zibanejad has the best chance of a point at 67%. Ice Sheet's under-the-radar pick is Oliver Bjorkstrand, a fourth-liner with dangerous shots lately: 16% to score, against a Toronto defence that gives up a lot of chances.
